chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
When this world advances towards anyone, it attributes to him the good qualities of others; and when it turns away from him, it deprives him of his own good qualities.

key_terms.أَعَارَتْهُ: It lent him / attributed to him

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of worldly favor on a person's perceived virtues according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this profound aphorism from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the transient nature of worldly status (*dunya*) as a divine test that often obscures true character. He illustrates how external favor can temporarily 'borrow' virtues from others to elevate the favored, while its withdrawal strips away even one's inherent dignity, highlighting the fragility of worldly esteem compared to spiritual reality.
